title: Arc — Atomic Rc
narrative:
## Thread-Safe Shared Ownership

`Arc[T]` (Atomically Reference Counted) is the thread-safe version of `Rc`. Use it to share data across threads.

### Arc vs Rc

| Feature | Rc | Arc |
|---------|-----|------|
| Thread safe | No | Yes |
| Performance | Faster | Slower (atomic ops) |
| Use case | Single thread | Multiple threads |
| API | Same | Same |

### Creating and Using Arc

```xiom
let shared = Arc.new(Vec[Int]());
shared.push(42);

let clone1 = shared.clone();  // atomic increment
let clone2 = shared.clone();  // atomic increment

// Safe to pass to threads
// thread::spawn(|| { let data = clone1; ... });
// thread::spawn(|| { let data = clone2; ... });
```

### Arc is Read-Only

Like Rc, Arc provides shared read access. For mutation across threads, combine with `Mutex` or `RwLock`:

```xiom
// Arc + Mutex = thread-safe mutable shared state
let counter = Arc.new(Mutex.new(0));
```

### Reference Counting

```xiom
let arc = Arc.new(100);
let refs = arc.ref_count();  // 1

let a2 = arc.clone();
let refs2 = arc.ref_count();  // 2
```

### When to Use Arc

- Sharing data between threads
- Concurrent data structures
- Any time multiple threads need to own the same data

### Performance Note

Arc's atomic operations are slower than Rc's non-atomic ones. Use Rc when you don't need thread safety.
tips: Use Arc for thread-safe shared ownership — atomic reference counting
Use Rc for single-threaded shared ownership — faster, non-atomic
Arc::clone() is cheap — it just increments an atomic counter
Combine Arc with Mutex/RwLock for thread-safe mutation
